title: Invertibility of the resolution-defined qcqs flat base-change map
statement: For f:X→S quasi-compact and quasi-separated, g:S′→S flat, g′=pullback.snd g f flat, F a quasi-coherent O_X-module, I and J injective resolutions of F and g′*F, t:I→g′_*J an augmentation-preserving comparison lift, and p≥0, the specific sheaf morphism flatBaseChangeResolutionBeta f g I J t p is an isomorphism. This is the actual O_X-module-derived comparison, for arbitrary flat base change, not only an Ext cohomology dimension identity over field extensions. source.place: Lemma 30.5.2, part (1) and its proof: affine-local reduction, separated Cech proof and the qcqs Cech-to-cohomology spectral sequence; comparison map from 02N7.

proof.text: Prove the scalar-extension comparison H.baseChange bijective for every compact quasi-separated scheme over any commutative ring and any flat commutative algebra. Use Mathlib compact_open_induction_on. The induction property quantifies over every open immersion with prescribed image and every quasi-coherent coefficient on its domain, so the induction hypothesis applies to the pulled-back open in each gluing step. The empty open has empty domain, hence the separated case applies. In the step adjoining an affine open C to a compact open A, their overlap is compact by quasi-separatedness and separated because it is open in the affine C. Apply the separated comparison to C and A intersect C, the induction hypothesis to A, and the Mayer-Vietoris gluing comparison to A union C. At the top open specialize to the identity immersion. This is the private proved helper flatCohomologyBaseChange_bijective.

The affine opens W in S prime contained in g inverse V for some affine V in S form a basis: first choose V around g(x), then choose affine W inside the given neighbourhood intersect g inverse V. For each such W, the map A=Gamma(S,V)→B=Gamma(S prime,W) is flat by Scheme.Hom.flat_appLE. The scheme f inverse V is compact by quasi-compactness of f and quasi-separated by quasi-separatedness of the restricted f over the affine V. Its restricted coefficient is quasi-coherent. Apply the previous step to its canonical map to Spec A and flat algebra B. The new affine-section dictionary identifies the resulting bijectivity with that of the actual resolution-defined beta on W, for the given augmented lift t.

Use ConcreteCategory.isIso_iff_bijective to turn each local bijectivity into invertibility in AddCommGrpCat. Apply TopCat.Sheaf.isIso_iff_isIso_basis to the underlying abelian-sheaf morphism on this basis. Its components on every open are therefore invertible. Scheme.Modules.Hom.isIso_iff_isIso_app reflects these component isomorphisms to the original module-sheaf morphism beta.

theorem Scheme.Modules.flatBaseChangeResolutionBeta_isIso
    {X S S' : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (g : S' ⟶ S)
    [QuasiCompact f] [QuasiSeparated f] [Flat g] [Flat (pullback.snd g f)]
    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent]
    (I : InjectiveResolution F)
    (J : InjectiveResolution
      ((Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback (pullback.snd g f)).obj F))
    (t : I.cocomplex ⟶
      ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward (pullback.snd g f)).mapHomologicalComplex
        (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).obj J.cocomplex)
    (ht : I.ι.f 0 ≫ t.f 0 =
      (Classical.choose (Scheme.Modules.exists_tensorPullbackAdjunction
        (pullback.snd g f))).unit.app F ≫
          (Scheme.Modules.pushforward (pullback.snd g f)).map (J.ι.f 0)) (p : ℕ) :
    IsIso (Scheme.Modules.flatBaseChangeResolutionBeta f g I J t p)
